scope: Primary Linux kernel and Linux man-pages references for the separate live-sibling observer; no source is asserted to describe the exact host kernel build.

sources.title: clone(2)
sources.supports: Same-thread-group tasks share TGID and parentage. CLONE_THREAD requires CLONE_SIGHAND, which requires CLONE_VM on modern Linux. This is the reason one live sibling represents the shared address space rather than adding another process contribution.

sources.title: pthread_exit(3)
sources.supports: Exiting the calling thread does not itself terminate all other threads or release all process-shared resources.

sources.title: proc_pid_task(5)
sources.supports: Task directories are named by TID and expose per-task attributes. The documentation warns that the directory may be unavailable after the main thread terminates; the candidate requires successful complete reads instead of assuming availability.

sources.title: proc_pid_status(5)
sources.supports: Tgid identifies the thread group, Pid identifies the task, and Threads gives the process thread count; State describes task state.

sources.title: The /proc Filesystem
sources.supports: smaps_rollup aggregates mapping statistics for the process. These observations remain non-atomic and do not prove an absolute peak.

sources.title: fs/proc/task_mmu.c
sources.supports: The rollup reads the selected task's memory context and can return ESRCH when the context or task is unavailable. The shared address-space interpretation comes from clone semantics; host behavior is separately demonstrated by the C witness.
